input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’m not sure about the mobile data part, but I just checked my phone and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something? I haven’t tried making calls or sending regular texts since this started. Should I try that now?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode and now the little airplane icon is gone. I see some bars for signal, and something that says "2G" at the top. Should I try making a call or sending a text now?
I just tried, and I can send a regular text message, but I still can’t send a picture message. Is it because of that "2G" thing you mentioned? What should I do next?

Alright, I switched my phone to the 4G/5G option, and now it says "5G" at the top with full bars. But I still can’t send a picture message—it’s just not working. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there isn’t anything listed for the MMSC URL. I’m not really sure what that means. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I need to do? I’d appreciate some guidance, since this is all a bit confusing for me.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. 

I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I really don’t want to lose anything important.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it already has access to both storage and SMS. Is there anything else that could be causing the problem?
Oh, I see! That makes sense now. Yes, I’d like to add 2GB of data, please. Can you confirm the total cost before you go ahead with it? I just want to make sure I understand.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. I’d like to get this working again. Thank you for explaining everything!
Great news—I just tried, and now I’m able to send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help and patience. I really appreciate you walking me through everything.

Thank you! I’ll do that. Have a wonderful day yourself, and thanks again for all your help. Goodbye! 

###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD), or

First, can you confirm:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send/receive standard text messages (SMS)?

I’m not sure about the mobile data part, but I just checked my phone and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something? I haven’t tried making calls or sending regular texts since this started. Should I try that now?

The airplane icon means Airplane Mode is enabled, which turns off all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data. This would prevent you from sending MMS, making calls, or sending texts.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. After you do that, try making a regular call or sending a standard text message to confirm your service is restored. Let me know if you’re able to do that, and if the airplane icon disappears.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode and now the little airplane icon is gone. I see some bars for signal, and something that says "2G" at the top. Should I try making a call or sending a text now?

Yes, please try making a regular call or sending a standard text message to confirm your basic service is working. 

Also, since your phone is showing "2G," this network type is generally not suitable for sending MMS (picture messages). Once you confirm that calls or texts are working, I’ll guide you to switch your network mode to a faster option (like 4G or 5G) to help with MMS.

Let me know if your call or text goes through!
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, and I can send a regular text message, but I still can’t send a picture message. Is it because of that "2G" thing you mentioned? What should I do next?

Yes, being on "2G" is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages (MMS), as 2G networks are generally not suitable for MMS.

To fix this, you’ll need to change your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G. Please go to your phone’s network settings and select the option for “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G preferred.” 

Once you’ve changed the network mode, check if your phone now shows “4G,” “LTE,” or “5G” at the top. Then, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you need help finding the network settings, or if changing the mode helps!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred

Alright, I switched my phone to the 4G/5G option, and now it says "5G" at the top with full bars. But I still can’t send a picture message—it’s just not working. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for updating your network mode. Since you’re now on 5G with full signal but still can’t send MMS, let’s check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed. If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the steps or suggest resetting your APN settings to default, which often resolves this issue.

Would you like instructions to check or reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there isn’t anything listed for the MMSC URL. I’m not really sure what that means. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I need to do? I’d appreciate some guidance, since this is all a bit confusing for me.

Thank you for checking. If the MMSC URL is missing, that’s likely why MMS isn’t working. The best next step is to reset your APN settings to their default values. This should restore the correct MMSC URL and other necessary settings for MMS.

Please go to your phone’s APN settings and select the option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” After you reset the APN settings, you’ll need to restart (reboot) your phone for the changes to take effect.

Once you’ve done both steps—resetting the APN and rebooting your phone—try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone model, or if you run into any issues during this process.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. 

I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Rest assured, rebooting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, allowing new settings (like the APN changes) to take effect.

It’s a safe and common step in troubleshooting. Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. If you have any concerns or run into issues after rebooting, let me know—I’m here to help!

Next, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your device, as this can sometimes interfere with sending MMS. Could you please check your phone’s settings and let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? If it is, please turn it off and then try sending a picture message again.

Please check your messaging app’s permissions in your phone’s settings. Make sure that both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled for the app you use to send messages.

If either permission is missing, please enable it and then try sending a picture message again. Let me know if both permissions are already enabled, or if you need help finding these settings.
